name: Would changing the bathroom door make my small bathroom work better?

mainEntity.name: Would changing the bathroom door make my small bathroom work better?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A door that swings into a small bathroom can consume the room’s most useful floor area and interfere with the toilet or vanity. Reversing the swing, using a pocket door, or changing the opening may help, but each option depends on wall space, privacy, structure, hardware, and local requirements.

Elite Remodeling & Design can evaluate the entry as part of the full layout instead of treating it as a separate finish decision. The design should show the door open and closed alongside the shower, vanity, and toilet.

Key factors:
- Available wall cavity for a pocket door
- Structural and utility conflicts
- Door clearance and privacy
- Hallway and adjacent-room impacts

Tape the door arc on the floor and check the approach from the hallway. Ask for the complete opening detail before ordering a door or moving a wall.
acceptedAnswer.description: It may recover valuable floor area, especially when the door conflicts with the vanity or toilet. Compare swing reversal, pocket, and other options against wall space, utilities, structure, privacy, hallway clearance, and the complete room layout.
